summary: A worked example of using IBM TSO at UCLA CCN over the network. It walks through logging on, creating a Fortran source with the editor, and running a batch compilation and foreground execution, with annotations explaining each step.

plainLanguage.summary: A step-by-step demo of using a big computer: log in, write a small program, run it and see the answer, with notes beside each step.

questions: how to compile fortran in tso
what is foreground execution in tso
subtitle: A worked example of batch compilation and foreground execution in TSO.

tldr.problem: Researchers needed to see how to use TSO's combined batch and foreground execution for real tasks.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 390 walks through a complete scenario: logging on with a user ID and password, creating a Fortran source file with EDIT, submitting it to batch compilation, and running the compiled program interactively in the foreground.
tldr.outcome: Network users could understand the full workflow of editing, compiling and running a Fortran program on UCLA CCN's TSO.

today: RFC 390 is Unknown status. It is a historical worked example showing how to use TSO at UCLA CCN in August 1972 for interactive computing over the ARPANET.

sections.title: Login and File Creation
sections.content: The scenario starts with logon using a TSO user ID and password. After the login sequence, the user enters the EDIT command to create a new Fortran source file named SAMPLE with a FORTG specification (which sets logical tabs correctly for Fortran). The EDIT command enters INPUT mode automatically for a new file, and the user types line numbers as prompts while entering lines. The example is a simple Fortran program that reads a number, computes its square root, and prints the result, with an infinite loop to accept multiple inputs.
sections.plainLanguage: The user logs in with a password, then uses the EDIT tool to type a Fortran program line by line.

sections.title: Batch Submission and Execution
sections.content: After editing and saving the source file, the user allocates a load module library dataset and then submits the source file to batch using the SUBMIT command. TSO prompts for a job name (P in this case), creates job ABC123P, and the user monitors the job's status through the STATUS command. The batch job runs the FORTGCL procedure to compile the Fortran code. Once the job finishes, the user examines the output using EDIT and a FIND command to locate the return code. BBN's system shows the compilation was successful (return code 0).
sections.plainLanguage: The user tells TSO to compile the program in the background. TSO gives it a job number and the user can ask how it is going. After a minute, the job finishes and the user can read the result.

sections.title: Running the Program
sections.content: With the compiled program ready, the user allocates input and output files to the terminal using ALLOCATE FILE commands, then uses the CALL command to run the compiled load module. The program prompts for input and the user enters two test values (3.141 and 4096), receiving the correct square root results. The user then types another value to re-enter the loop, and finally hits READY to exit the program, followed by LOGOFF to end the TSO session.
sections.plainLanguage: The user runs the compiled program right there at the terminal, types in some numbers, watches it calculate square roots, and logs off.

references.text: RFC 377, Using TSO VIA ARPA Network Virtual Terminal
